newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Guinness sees tough European market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Guinness sees tough European market.

text.p: British brewing and spirits group Guinness Plc turned in half year results above expectations on Thursday but chairman Tony Greener said markets in Europe were tough and not expected to change this year.

Guinness turned in a five percent rise in pretax profits for the six months ending June 30 of 357 million pounds ($556.4 million) and above expectations of 337 to 353 million pounds. It paid out an interim dividend of 4.55 pence per share, up from 4.20 pence previously.

Guinness shares fell 6p to 446p as doubts rose about the company's spirits sales -- Scotch Whisky sales were four percent behind last year at 10.2 million cases, mainly due to de-stocking in Latin American markets.

"The company has committed itself to a substantial increase in spending on advertising and promotion in the second half but it is living in hope that sales will increase to offset that," said Charles Winston, analyst at BZW.

Greener said in an interview that overall, spirits prices were up 0.5 percent in the first half of the year to June 30 compared with the same period last year, but the full year effect would be a two percent increase on last year, he said.
Guinness got a three percent price rise through in spirits in the United States during the half year, four percent in Britain but achieved only very little in Asia.

"The future of the business lies in brands and building brands," said Greener. At United Distillers, the company's spirits arm, the group will spend 20 percent more this year on promoting its brands. It spent about 300 million pounds last year on spirits marketing.

"We are not only putting the total amount of money up but we are switching money in the mix to focus on brand building (media advertising) activities and taking it away from price promotion and price volume support.
In Britain, Guinness will launch a national television advertisement for both Bell's whisky and Gordon's gin in the run up to Christmas.
Greener said Guinness is taking a "very tough line" by cutting back on price promotions and investing more heavily in brands like Bell's.

"In the UK we are just utterly determined to make sure that our major brands are built in terms of their appeal to the consumer. That's why we are using television now for the first time and we are seeing some very good results from that."
"The acid test in the UK is going to be what happens at Christmas where we are very strongly determined not to get into major price promotional activities," Greener added.
"And we have stated our position clearly and we very much hope that the rest of the industry take a similarly robust point of view."
A strong performance in Asia enabled UD to report flat profits of 255 million pounds in the first half.

Trading profit from the Asia Pacific region rose to 65 million pounds up from 51 million. Profits from spirits sales in Britain fell four million to 16 million and by 10 million to 59 million in North America.

Guinness stout's share of the draft beer market in Britain, where spending on marketing has been high, reached a record five percent this year and continues to rise -- the brewing arm posted a five percent rise in profits to 119 million pounds. ($1=.6416 Pound)
